questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are present and working.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol while driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol. It is dangerous to you and to everyone else on the road.

questions.question: If stopped by police while driving in the District of Columbia, you must show your valid driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.
questions.explanation: You must provide your valid driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance when stopped by police in the District of Columbia. Failure to do so may result in a fine or arrest.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal to warn other drivers. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has flashing red lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think the children are done.
Slow down to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop until the red lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the red lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus has flashing red lights. Stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. If the bus is on the other side of a divided highway, you do not need to stop.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road

questions.explanation: Speed that is too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the dog is helping them cross the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes (with or without a red tip).

questions.question: A school bus ahead on your side of the road has flashing red lights. You must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: The flashing lights and stop arm on a school bus mean students are getting on or off. Do not go until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is put away. Never pass a school bus that is loading or unloading students.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming in both directions ahead.

questions.question: What is a sign of a drunk driver?
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slower than normal traffic, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they must drive in one direction on this street.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms your judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It has no effect on judgment but it harms driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your judgment of speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving may be reduced by:
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: You should yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the circumstances are.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Ensure that your tires have good tread depth.
Ensure that your tires are properly inflated.
Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition with proper tread and correct air pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at high speeds.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" is a driving condition that can result from:

options.text: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
Too much sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead at the road for too long without looking around you. This can cause you to zone out and miss traffic that is slowing down or stopping ahead of you.

questions.question: Driving under the influence of any medication that impairs your driving is permitted:

options.text: If it is prescribed by a physician.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your ability to drive safely. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce road rage?

options.text: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws and signals. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. This means drivers need to focus completely on driving. Any extra task can be dangerous.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. If you feel tired, stop driving right away.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: It is not safe to pass here.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass here.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass another car in a "No passing zone." These signs are used in areas where you cannot see far ahead. Passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and rest or have another driver take over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or have another driver take over.
questions.explanation: Take breaks every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can rest while they drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use their left arm held straight out to show they are turning left.
